basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 36.' and it opens '(Vers. 36.) Madianaei autem vendiderunt Joseph in Egypto Phutiphar eunucho, Pharaonis'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 36.) Madianaei autem vendiderunt Joseph in Egypto Phutiphar eunucho, Pharaonis archimagiro. In plerisque locis archimagiros, id est, coquorum principes, pro magistris exercitus Scriptura commemorat: μαγειρεύειν quippe Graece interpretatur occidere. Venditus est igitur Joseph principi exercitus et bellatorum, non Petephre, ut in Latino scriptum est, sed Phutiphar eunucho. Ubi quaeritur, quomodo postea uxorem habere dicatur. Tradunt Hebraei emptum ab hoc Joseph ob nimiam pulchritudinem in turpe ministerium, et a Domino virilibus ejus arefactis, postea electum esse juxta morem Hierophantarum in pontificatum Heliopoleos; et hujus filiam esse Aseneth, quam postea Joseph uxorem acceperit.
